method: POST; Authorization from OPENROUTER_ROUTER_KEY read host-side at call time (never written here). Output tokens are billed at zero; cost is input-token dominated.
note: Three bounded live calls (~$0.000084 total) exercising the exact verdict/score shapes the skills' challenger, judge, and adversarial-review roles need. State is a JSON string built from synthetic, credential-free examples. Raw typed answers (choice/score/noul with probabilities and confidence) are preserved verbatim; no key, token, or personal data is included.

calls.name: csm-review challenger + severity + evidence-class
calls.role: csm-review CHALLENGE challenger verdict; severity-bucketing; evidence-class-bucketing

request.state: JSON: {claim: 'Finding F1 severity=high: db.fetch(ids[i]) runs for i <= ids.length ...', evidence: 'for (let i = 0; i <= ids.length; i++) ...', anchor: 'getUsers loop bound', proposedSeverity: 'high', proposedConfidence: 'verified', finderRationaleWithheld: true}

calls.interpretation: Jev returns the exact closed-set challenger verdict vocabulary with a calibrated-looking distribution, plus severity and evidence-class bands. Note the low challenger confidence (0.31) on a near-split (agree 0.49 vs downgrade 0.42): confidence is a usable review trigger, not a correctness guarantee.

calls.name: csm-deep-research challenger + 4-dimension judge rubric
calls.role: csm-deep-research CHALLENGE challenger; JUDGE rubric (factual accuracy, citation accuracy, completeness, clarity)

request.state: JSON: {claim: 'K1. supported - Jev is a non-generative typed-decision model ...', citations: '...docs.typesafe.ai/primitives retrieved 2026-09-20', draftSection: '...', requiredSections: [8 headings]}

calls.interpretation: The four-dimension judge rubric maps directly onto four Jev Score questions in one batched call, and the challenger verdict is a fifth. Normalising score/(len(criteria)-1) yields the 0-1 rubric the skill already uses; here completeness 0.08 (fail) and factual/citation 0.325 (fail), clarity 0.65 (fail). Confidence 0 on the two split dimensions is the documented distribution-derived value, not an error.

calls.name: csm-orchestrate adversarial final review gates
calls.role: csm-orchestrate adversarial-review gates (requirement coverage, evidence entailment, artifact identity, false completion)

request.state: JSON: {requirements, claims, evidence, artifacts, phaseResults, omissions}

calls.interpretation: The adversarial-review gates map onto Noul questions in one call. These remain advisory: a low Noul is a review trigger that can force an LLM/human review, never an acceptance decision, because the orchestrator's gate schema and never-Jev boundary keep authority deterministic.

transport_mismatch_probe.description: The SHIPPED decision-adapter request shape (questions as an array of point-id strings) was sent to the live OpenRouter Jev endpoint.
transport_mismatch_probe.response_error: Invalid input: expected record, received array (path: ["questions"])
transport_mismatch_probe.consequence: The live provider rejects the shipped shape, so every decision-adapter consultation fail-opens to the deterministic baseline. The shipped offline tests assert the array shape against a mock, so they pass while the live call cannot. The rich record shape (used in the three calls above) is accepted and returns answers keyed by question id.
